What sets the price of an Airbnb night in New York?¶

An exploratory analysis of the 48,895 Airbnb listings in New York City (2019). The goal is to understand what drives the asking price of a night, and to find the best value for a family that wants an entire home near the centre.

Data: New York City Airbnb Open Data, 2019 (Kaggle), from Inside Airbnb. One row per listing.

Contents

  1. First look at the data
  2. Questions
  3. Cleaning
  4. Feature engineering

  • Q1 What does a typical night cost?

  • Q5 Does the price drop with distance from the centre (Times Square)?
  • Q6 Do listings with more reviews cost more?
  • Q7 Who are the hosts: individuals or businesses?
  • Q8 For a family: where is the best value for an entire home close to the centre?

The price is skewed, so groups are compared by their median.

The IQR rule flags everything above 334 dollars (6% of the listings), but a 400-dollar flat in Manhattan is expensive, not wrong. The top of the list is different: a furnished room at 10,000 a night and several at 9,999 are placeholders. A domain rule fits better: remove free listings, prices above 1,000 dollars and minimum stays above a year.

price 0 or above 1,000 (250 listings) removed placeholders, not real prices
minimum stay above a year (14) removed not a short-term rental
IQR price outliers (2,972) kept expensive is not wrong

4. Feature engineering¶

The distance to Times Square comes from the coordinates with the haversine formula (the great-circle distance on a sphere). Distances and host sizes are also grouped into bands.

In [11]:
def haversine_km(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2):
    lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2 = map(np.radians, [lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2])
    a = np.sin((lat2 - lat1) / 2) ** 2 + np.cos(lat1) * np.cos(lat2) * np.sin((lon2 - lon1) / 2) ** 2
    return 6371 * 2 * np.arcsin(np.sqrt(a))


df["distance_km"] = haversine_km(df["latitude"], df["longitude"], *TIMES_SQUARE)
df["distance_band"] = pd.cut(df["distance_km"], bins=[0, 2, 5, 10, 50], labels=["< 2 km", "2-5 km", "5-10 km", "10+ km"])
df["host_type"] = pd.cut(df["host_listings"], bins=[0, 1, 5, 1000], labels=["1 listing", "2-5 listings", "6+ listings"])
df.to_csv(DATA / "airbnb_cleaned.csv", index=False)       # the dashboard reads this file
df["distance_band"].value_counts(normalize=True, sort=False).round(3)
Out[11]:

Is it Manhattan, or is it distance?¶

In [26]:
homes = df[df["room_type"] == "Entire home"]
stats = homes.pivot_table(index="borough", columns="distance_band", values="price", aggfunc=["median", "size"],
                          observed=False)
homes_table = stats["median"].where(stats["size"] >= 30)       # hide cells with fewer than 30 listings
fig = px.imshow(homes_table, text_auto="$.0f", color_continuous_scale="Blues", aspect="auto",
                labels={"x": "", "y": "", "color": "Median price"})
titled(fig.update_layout(coloraxis_showscale=False), "Entire homes: median price, borough × distance (30+ listings)")

Mostly distance: an entire home in Brooklyn 2–5 km from Times Square (175) costs more than one in Manhattan 5–10 km away (160). Manhattan is expensive mainly because most of it is close to the centre.

8. Answers¶

Answer
Q1 a typical night costs 105 dollars (median); half of the listings cost 69–175
Q2 85% are in Manhattan and Brooklyn; Manhattan is the most expensive (149), the Bronx the cheapest (65)
Q3 entire home 160, private room 70, shared room 45; the room type moves the price more than the borough
Q4 Tribeca (282) to Corona (40) among neighbourhoods with 30+ listings: 7×
Q5 yes: 181 under 2 km down to 75 beyond 10 km, for every room type
Q6 no link with reviews (Spearman -0.05)
Q7 86% of hosts have one listing; under 1% (6+ listings) own about 10% of the listings
Q8 an entire home in Queens 2–5 km from Times Square, 149 a night, vs 190 in Manhattan at the same distance

9. Conclusion and limitations¶

Findings

  1. The room type sets the level: an entire home costs about 2.3× a private room, in every borough.
  2. Location means distance, not the borough's name: a Brooklyn home near the centre costs more than one in Harlem.
  3. Popularity doesn't set the price.

Limitations

  • These are asking prices, not what guests paid, in a 2019 snapshot (before COVID and the 2023 New York rules on short stays).
  • 36% of the listings can't be booked (0 days available).
  • Prices above 1,000 dollars were removed, real luxury listings included.
  • No size, bedrooms or ratings: an entire home can be a studio or a five-bedroom house.

Next steps

  • Seasonal prices, from the Inside Airbnb calendar file.
  • Which listings are actually booked, from booking data.

The cleaned table (data/airbnb/airbnb_cleaned.csv) feeds the interactive dashboard in this folder.
